tex_content.html:
Proposition
[Slice Coordinates] ↗ thm:rank-theorem 1. chA:A.22

Let $\tilde{M}$ be a smooth $m$-manifold without boundary and let $M \subseteq \tilde{M}$ be an embedded $n$-dimensional submanifold with or without boundary. Then for each $p \in M$ there exist a neighborhood $\tilde{U}$ of $p$ in $\tilde{M}$ and smooth coordinates $(x^1, \ldots , x^m)$ for $\tilde{M}$ on $\tilde{U}$ such that $M \cap \tilde{U}$ is a set of one of the following forms: \[ M \cap \tilde{U} = \begin{cases} \{ x \in \tilde{U} : x^{n+1} = \cdots = x^m = 0\} & \text{if } p \notin \partial M, \\ \{ x \in \tilde{U} : x^{n+1} = \cdots = x^m = 0 \text{ and } x^n \geq 0\} & \text{if } p \in \partial M. \end{cases} \]

In such a chart, $(x^1, \ldots , x^n)$ form smooth local coordinates for $M$.

Coordinates satisfying either of these conditions are called slice coordinates; when it is necessary to distinguish them, coordinates satisfying the second condition are referred to as boundary slice coordinates.

If $M$ is an immersed submanifold, then Theorem A.16 shows that every point of $M$ has a neighborhood $U$ in $M$ that is embedded in $\bar{M}$, so we can construct slice coordinates for $U$ (but they need not be slice coordinates for $M$).
